content.value_statement: Software teams need a repeatable path from project setup to deployment. This skill organizes development work into phased prompts and quality gates.
actual_capabilities: Breaks application work into setup, frontend, backend, database, testing, review, and deployment phases.
Lists companion skills to use for each phase of a development project.
Provides copy-paste prompts for common application development tasks.
Defines quality gates for tests, reviews, security scans, linting, and documentation.
Maps technology-specific workflows for React, Next.js, FastAPI, Node.js, mobile, and full-stack projects.
limitations: It does not implement code or run project commands by itself.
It depends on referenced companion skills being available in the user environment.
It gives workflow guidance, not framework-specific API documentation.
It does not validate production infrastructure or secrets configuration.

use_cases.title: Plan a new product build
use_cases.description: Turn an application idea into phases, companion skills, and quality gates before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Coordinate full-stack feature delivery
use_cases.description: Guide frontend, backend, database, and testing work for one feature across multiple contributors.

use_cases.title: Standardize release checks
use_cases.description: Use repeatable review, security, testing, and deployment gates before shipping application changes.

prompt_templates.title: Start a project plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the development workflow to plan a new [web/mobile/full-stack] application. Recommend phases, companion skills, and quality gates.

prompt_templates.title: Build a frontend feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend phase to plan a [feature name] in [framework]. Include component architecture, state, styling, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Add backend and database work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the backend and database phases for [feature name]. Cover API design, schema changes, authentication, errors, and integration tests.

prompt_templates.title: Run release readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the quality and deployment phases to prepare [project name] for release. Include review, security scans, CI, deployment, and documentation.

output_examples.input: Plan a new React and Node.js application.
output: A phased delivery plan covering setup, frontend, backend, database, tests, review, and deployment.
Recommended companion skills for React, Node.js, TypeScript, testing, and CI workflows.
Quality gates for linting, security scanning, documentation, and release readiness.
A checklist for tests, code review, security scans, linting, and documentation updates.
Deployment preparation steps for build pipelines, environment variables, and production validation.

output_examples.input: Choose companion skills for a mobile app.
output: A mobile workflow that references React Native, Flutter, iOS, backend, database, and testing support.
A recommended order for planning, implementation, quality review, and deployment.

best_practices: State the project type, target stack, and delivery goal before invoking the workflow.
Use the phase order, then adapt it for project risk and team maturity.
Run quality gates before moving from implementation to deployment.
anti_patterns: Using every referenced skill when the task only needs one phase.
Skipping testing and review phases to move directly to deployment.
Treating generic workflow prompts as a substitute for project-specific requirements.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and prompts for other development skills.

faq.question: Which tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it build both frontend and backend work?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers frontend, backend, database, testing, review, and deployment phases.

faq.question: Does it include mobile development?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a mobile workflow that references React Native, Flutter, and iOS skills.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for framework documentation?
faq.answer: No. It helps organize work, but framework details still require current official documentation.

faq.question: How should teams use it safely?
faq.answer: Review suggested prompts, choose only needed phases, and run normal code review and security checks.
